diseases.name: Bacterial Leaf Blight
diseases.favorable_conditions: High humidity (70-90%), temperatures between 25-34°C, strong winds and continuous rain.
diseases.short_desc: Water-soaked lesions on leaf tips and margins that turn yellowish-white with wavy margins, leading to rapid blighting.
symptoms: Water-soaked stripes along leaf margins starting from tips
Lesions turn yellowish-white with wavy edges as they enlarge
Milky or amber bacterial ooze droplets on leaves during early morning
Leaves wilt, roll, and turn grayish-green ('Kresek' phase in seedlings)
Severe yield reduction (up to 50-70%) during tillering to panicle stage
causes: Infection by bacteria Xanthomonas oryzae through leaf wounds or hydathodes
Excessive nitrogenous fertilization without balanced potassium
Deep standing water in nurseries and fields
Contaminated irrigation channels and infected crop stubble
diseases.spread_factors: Wind-driven rain, irrigation runoff, infected plant debris, volunteer rice plants, and weed hosts (e.g., Leersia hexandra).

diseases.name: Leaf Blast
diseases.favorable_conditions: Night temperatures 17-23°C, relative humidity >90%, prolonged leaf wetness (>10 hours), and heavy dew.
diseases.short_desc: Spindle-shaped or diamond-shaped lesions with gray or whitish centers and dark reddish-brown borders.
symptoms: Eye-shaped or diamond-shaped elliptical spots on leaves
Lesion center turns ash-gray or white with brownish or purple margin
Spots coalesce, causing entire leaf blades to wither and dry up ('blast burn')
Can attack collar, neck of panicles ('neck blast'), causing completely empty whiteheads
Severe field lodging and complete crop devastation if untreated
causes: Airborne fungal spores (conidia) produced in millions on infected leaves
Heavy applications of synthetic nitrogen fertilizer
Drought stress followed by sudden wet cool spells
High planting density resulting in dense, microclimate canopy
diseases.spread_factors: Air currents, wind, dew drops, infected crop residue, susceptible wild grasses.

diseases.name: Brown Spot
diseases.favorable_conditions: Nutrient-deficient soils (especially low silicon, potassium, zinc), temperature 20-30°C, and prolonged cloudiness.
diseases.short_desc: Circular to oval dark brown lesions with yellow halo, heavily linked to poor soil nutrition and drought stress.
symptoms: Small, circular to oval dark brown spots on leaves and glumes
Larger spots develop a gray or light brown center surrounded by yellow chlorotic halo
Infected grains become discolored, spotted, and shriveled ('pecky rice')
Severe seedling blight leading to poor plant stand in dry seedbeds
causes: Associated with poor soil fertility, zinc deficiency, drought stress, or silicon deficiency
Fungal pathogen Bipolaris oryzae surviving in seed coat and stubble
Nutrient imbalance and light sandy soils lacking organic matter
diseases.spread_factors: Infected seeds, airborne spores, contaminated crop residue, water stress.

diseases.name: Leaf Smut
diseases.favorable_conditions: High humidity, mature crop stage, moderate temperature (24-28°C), and high nitrogen.
diseases.short_desc: Small, angular black spots slightly raised on both leaf surfaces, mostly visible as the crop matures.
symptoms: Small, slightly raised angular black spots (sori) scattered across leaf blades
Spots are covered by the leaf epidermis and do not rupture easily
Affected leaves turn prematurely yellow and dry up from tips
Typically appears late in the growing season during milky to grain maturity stages
causes: Entyloma oryzae fungus surviving in soil and old crop debris
Late season high humidity and shaded plant canopies
Over-use of urea late in the vegetative phase
diseases.spread_factors: Wind-borne teliospores, irrigation wash, infected straw.

diseases.name: Tungro
diseases.favorable_conditions: Abundance of Green Leafhopper (Nephotettix virescens), temperature 25-30°C, presence of stubbles from previous infected crop.
diseases.short_desc: Severe stunting, yellow-orange leaf discoloration, reduced tillering, delayed flowering, and sterile panicles.
symptoms: Severe stunting of plant height and drastically reduced tillering
Leaves turn yellow to vivid orange-yellow starting from the tips down the margins
Young leaves mottled or with pale green to white interveinal stripes
Panicles small, poorly exerted, with high proportion of empty grains
Stunted patches visible randomly across the field
causes: Co-infection of Rice Tungro Bacilliform Virus (RTBV) and Rice Tungro Spherical Virus (RTSV)
Transmitted non-persistently by the Green Leafhopper (Nephotettix virescens)
Continuous staggered planting creating a non-stop green bridge for leafhoppers
diseases.spread_factors: Green leafhopper vectors hopping from plant to plant, weed hosts, overlapping crop seasons.

diseases.name: Sheath Blight
diseases.favorable_conditions: High relative humidity (85-100%), temperature 28-32°C, dense foliage canopy, and heavy nitrogen application.
diseases.short_desc: Oval or snake-skin lesions on leaf sheaths near water line that expand upward to leaf blades, causing lodging.
symptoms: Initial lesions on leaf sheaths just above the water level
Spots are greenish-gray, oval or irregular with distinctive brown to dark purple margins
Lesions coalesce, creating a banded or 'snake-skin' appearance along the sheath
Infection travels upward to upper leaves and panicles in dense stands
Tillers die, panicles fail to fill, and severe lodging occurs
causes: Soil-borne sclerotia of Rhizoctonia solani that float on irrigation water
Excessive plant population (>50 hills/m²) and high nitrogen doses (>150 kg N/ha)
Stagnant water and humid dense canopy microclimate
diseases.spread_factors: Floating sclerotia in irrigation water, vegetative mycelial growth across adjacent tillers, infested soil.

diseases.name: Healthy Paddy Leaf
diseases.favorable_conditions: Balanced nutrient management, good irrigation drainage, clean seed, and periodic field monitoring.
diseases.short_desc: Vibrant emerald green leaves with uniform coloration, intact smooth margins, strong erect stems, and no visible lesions.
symptoms: Uniform, vibrant green or dark green leaf color
Clean, intact margins without necrotic spots or yellow striping
Vigorous tillering and healthy white root system
Erect leaf canopy maximizing sunlight interception
causes: Optimal crop health, balanced N-P-K-Zn-Si nutrition, and proactive organic prophylaxis
